summary: Follow-up on Oct 31 production incident where Aurora Health experienced intermittent 5xxs and elevated tail latency for Redwood Dedicated pool. Discussed root cause, mitigations applied, evidence from telemetry, and next steps for improved reliability and security verification.
topics: Incident timeline and root cause (KV cache invalidation + retry amplification)
Mitigations applied (cache TTL fix, backoff changes, improved alerting)
Security/audit concerns around data retention and KMS
Longer-term reliability items (circuit breakers, autoscaling policy adjustments, canary routing)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood CSM), Darren (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Support), Liam (Aurora VP Eng), Sofia (Aurora Platform), Dev (On-call Eng), Nina (Aurora Security), Aaron (Product)

Summary: quick sync to confirm that the fixes Redwood pushed after the 2026-10-31 incident are working in staging and to align on verification steps and timeline for production re-rollout.

[00:00] Maya: okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, um, we'll run through the postmortem findings and then the mitigation steps, quick check on status, and then next steps.
[00:12] Liam: yeah thanks Maya, appreciate it. we had a pretty rough spike on the 31st, so looking to make sure this is actually fixed before broad rollout.
[00:25] Darren: sure, i'll run through what we found - quick caveat, some of the names in the automate logs got munged, so i'll try to call out the exact traces.
[00:35] Darren: timeline: around 03:14 UTC we saw errors start to rise on the dedicated pool for aurora-prod, both 5xx and 524-ish gateway timeouts. traces showed a pattern of kv cache invalidation on certain prefixes followed by a burst of origin requests which led to retry amplification on a downstream microservice.
[01:02] Dev: and those were the same requests that our on-call saw? the request IDs in our pager matched, yeah?
[01:10] Darren: yes, the request IDs aligned - we correlated the telemetry from our side and yours; there was a small window where the kv cache TTL rolled to zero in the cache node due to a bug in cache expiry logic when eviction combined with a particular sequence of partial writes.
[01:35] Dev: tricky, ok. so that caused a thundering herd?
[01:40] Darren: exactly, then our internal retry logic caused multiple attempts - some of which didn't have exponential backoff because the older code path got hit for specific error codes, so we had retry amplification. that pushed downstream latency up and produced 5xxs.
[02:05] Sofia: did the autoscaler not handle it? i thought dedicated pool autoscaling would spin up extra workers.
[02:12] Darren: autoscaling did kick in but the latency spike was faster than scale-up, and we hit a brief IO contention on the storage path for the downstream service; autoscale policy then thrash-sampled in a way that made it worse before stabilizing. we're recommending a couple of policy tweaks.
[02:30] Maya: quick question from product: Aaron, do you have baseline SLOs we want to guarantee for the re-roll?
[02:38] Aaron: we want p99 user-facing latency under 350ms and error rate under 0.1% over any 30m window. that's the bar we need to validate against in staging.
[02:50] Darren: noted. mitigation steps we pushed yesterday: 1) patched cache TTL logic to avoid zeroed TTL on partial eviction, 2) patched retry path to ensure exponential backoff for the legacy error code path, 3) added a circuit breaker on downstream calls to cap concurrent origin requests per node, 4) improved alerting rules to detect unusual cache miss bursts.
[03:22] Dev: can you confirm which commits and PRs? we need the SHA for our audit.
[03:28] Priya: yep, i'll paste the PRs in the notes after the call, we've got two PRs: redwood/infra#423 and redwood/runtime#2101.
[03:36] Nina: security side, i want to confirm there was no change to data retention or unexpected exports as part of the mitigations.
[03:43] Darren: no data exports, only config and runtime fixes; we did adjust a cache TTL default which doesn't change retention semantics. we'll provide a statement for audit.
[03:55] Nina: ok, also need to verify KMS key usage - were any keys rotated?
[03:59] Darren: no rotations; we tested rotation in staging but didn't rotate keys in prod.
[04:08] Liam: what about the telemetry - do you have the before/after charts?
[04:12] Darren: yes - i can share the dashboards. initial staging run shows error rate down to 0.03% and p99 at 280ms under a synthetic mix that replicates the customer traffic profile.
[04:30] Sofia: that synthetic mix - can you run it with our exact trace capture? we pointed out a couple of long-running sequences on our side that might behave differently.
[04:38] Darren: absolutely, we can run the recorded traffic replay you shared; Darren: (laugh) sorry, that was me saying absolutely.
[04:45] Aaron: one other ask - we need to see results for a sustained 30-minute run at 2x peak traffic to be comfortable.
[04:53] Darren: good, we'll schedule that. question for aurora - do you want the canary to be region-based or route-based?
[05:02] Sofia: route-based, we have a few critical routes. region-based would be fine too but routes give us more control.
[05:10] Darren: ok route-based canary. we'll set up a 5% traffic canary with auto-rollback on error rate threshold.
[05:18] Dev: back to the root cause - i'm curious if similar logic exists in other parts of your infra, like the private deployment path.
[05:25] Darren: we audited similar cache code paths in Private and Dedicated; Private uses our newer cache module so it's not impacted, Dedicated older runtime was the one affected. we've got a compatibility shim to prevent regressions.
[05:40] Maya: let's cover verification steps and owners now. Darren, run the list.
[05:45] Darren: verification checklist: 1) apply patch to staging (done), 2) replay aurora traffic capture in staging for 1h at 1x and 2x peak (owner: Darren), 3) run SS load test with 2x peak for 30m (owner: Darren), 4) collect and share dashboards + traces (owner: Darren/Priya), 5) security confirm KMS/audit (owner: Nina), 6) production canary rollout with 5% traffic and auto-rollback (owner: Maya/Darren).
[06:20] Maya: good. timeline - we want staging validation by end of next week. so timeline matches the next steps above.
[06:30] Sofia: for the replay, we need to make sure obfuscated PII is handled, the log capture has to be redacted.
[06:36] Darren: yep we'll use the redact tooling, and we'll only accept hashed IDs.
[06:42] Nina: also, we'll need an SOC 2 style note for post-deploy verification, can you include in the postmortem doc please?
[06:50] Maya: will do.
[07:00] Aaron: any thought on long-term changes? like is it worth changing retry policies globally or adding per-tenant circuit breakers?
[07:08] Darren: yes, long-term recommendations include per-customer circuit breakers, more conservative default retry policies, and better autoscaler hysteresis. also adding canary hooks in the routing layer so we can do traffic shaping rapidly.
[07:25] Dev: and more observability for kv cache hit/miss at the route level would help.
[07:30] Darren: agreed, adding route-level cache metrics is on the backlog - we can prioritize it for Aurora.
[07:38] Maya: ok let's open it up for questions.
[07:42] Sofia: what's the rollback plan if canary shows a 0.2% error spike?
[07:46] Darren: auto-rollback configured at 0.15% over 5m window; manual rollback steps are documented in the runbook we'll share.
[07:55] Liam: are there any customer-visible changes, like endpoint names or API semantics?
[07:59] Priya: none, all changes are internal runtime and config - we won't change endpoints.
[08:05] Nina: thanks, please include the audit logs export steps in the runbook.
[08:10] Darren: noted.
[08:15] Maya: quick recap - Maya: (formal) we'll share the consolidated postmortem and PR links by 2026-11-20; Darren will run the replay and load tests and share results by 2026-11-24; Nina to confirm KMS/audit by 2026-11-22; canary planned for week of 2026-11-29 pending results.
[08:42] Liam: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:46] Aaron: thanks, appreciate it.
[08:48] Maya: ok we'll follow up over email and update the CRM.

Notes/References:
- PRs: redwood/infra#423, redwood/runtime#2101 (will attach links)
